definition: A defined way for software components to exchange requests and responses.
A learned language model that generates or scores token sequences. Fluent output can still be incorrect.
Methods that learn patterns from data rather than requiring every decision to be written as a rule.
Retrieve relevant source material and provide it as context for generation. Retrieval and generation need separate evaluation.
A text format for structured data. Valid syntax does not establish correct values or authorization.
A request/response protocol used by web clients and services.
A simple comparison system used to judge whether added complexity improves the intended outcome.
Evaluation on examples kept separate from development and tuning. Repeatedly adapting to them weakens their independence.
Information unavailable at real prediction time enters development or evaluation and can inflate apparent performance.
A numeric representation used to compare or process items. Similarity is task-dependent and does not establish truth.
Establishing an identity using a trusted verification mechanism.
Deciding which resources or actions an established identity may access.
Rules specifying which identities or groups may access a resource.
A measurable target for a service property such as availability or latency, with a defined observation window.
Elapsed time for a defined operation. State whether you mean time to first output, full response time or another measure.
A change in data or relationships over time. A drift signal alone does not prove degraded task quality.
A repeatable check that detects specified behavior changing unexpectedly. Its coverage is limited to the properties checked.
Untrusted content attempts to redirect a model or agent. Protect permissions and action boundaries independently of prompt wording.
Controlled example data or setup used for a repeatable exercise or test.
Repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once, such as ingesting a record without creating duplicates.
